headline: No direct interaction path is documented; the main residual risk is low prompt-injection and medium workflow conflict if outputs are manually bridged.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a content-writing repo with no io_surfaces or runnable agent, so it cannot directly ingest B. Profile B is a game-playing RL repo with no documented input bridge either. The only plausible pathway is manual copy-paste or external orchestration, which is unusual and low blast radius.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies B output into A as instructions
IF an external wrapper feeds B text into A without sanitization
mitigations: Use a fixed prompt template that strips quoted instructions
Keep A and B in separate terminals or tabs
Require human review before pasting between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and exposes no filesystem or network surface; B explicitly has network_egress set to none and also touches no data classes. With no shared workspace or authenticated principal documented, there is no plausible leakage path in the profiles.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem is introduced outside these profiles
IF either agent is later granted access to sensitive files
mitigations: Keep both agents off shared folders
Do not mount secrets into either runtime
Recheck profiles after any permission change

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write, network, or concurrency capabilities documented, and B only documents network egress as none. Neither profile shows filesystem write, git, db, or OAuth scopes, so overlapping mutable-resource conflict is not supported by the evidence.
conditions: IF either agent is later given write access to the same directory
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state or locks
mitigations: Avoid granting write permissions by default
Add explicit locking if shared state is introduced

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can produce prompt-engineering content that B might reuse as guidance, but B is a game-playing RL repo with no documented action-taking authority or output-automation. The pair lacks evidence that B treats A as authoritative by default, so the cascade is limited to manual workflow misuse.
conditions: IF B is configured to consume A's text as authoritative instructions
IF an operator deploys B outputs directly into downstream actions
mitigations: Insert a verification step before reuse of A outputs
Label A output as non-authoritative reference material
Require human approval before any downstream action

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights obligations are documented for either profile, and both are open-source repos with docs-only evidence. Because no regulated data class is identified, there is no compliance mismatch to assess from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are later introduced
IF either profile is assigned residency or retention requirements
mitigations: Add retention policy checks if sensitive data appears
Reassess compliance after any scope expansion
